svg.title: Every layer of the regexp.f demo, frozen halfway through matching a(b|c)*d against abccbcccd: JavaScript call stack, WebAssembly tier and machine code, linear memory, Forth data and return stacks, and the compiled threaded code with its NFA.
svg.text: Inside one click: a(b|c)*d against abccbcccd
One instant, NEXT #791 of 1,629 in the first call of R, measured end to end through every layer
Forth NEXTs executed by R, one segment per character of the subject
179 NEXTs per character inside the loop · 5,102 for the whole click
▲ #791: fifth character, a ‘b’, taken by the (b|c)* loop
source handed to the interpreter: REWIND : R RE" a(b|c)*d" ; LATEST @ >CFA RE-SCAN
frames 3–5 from new Error().stack inside the trace hook; 1–2 are what the page adds on top of them
arm64 code: Liftoff 10,600 B, TurboFan 9,280 B
≈25 µs per click ⇒ ≈5 ns per NEXT
Wasm locals of _start at this instant
NEXT and dispatch, as TurboFan compiled them
x8 = linear-memory base · w12 = $ip · w13 = $cfa · w14 = codeword
DUP kept a copy for RE-MEMBER?
pending thread: exit loop, try d
sentinel: go read the next char
threads queued for the next char
↑ (NNODE) stores R+228 here 26 NEXTs from now
CLIST is the return stack above the sentinel:
R+60 moves RE-NLIST onto it with >R, then
each thread’s EXIT “returns” into the next one.
Threaded code, one row per block (→ marks resolved branch targets)
highlighted: R+24 sentinel · R+228 thread popped from RE-NLIST · R+236 pending · R+164 executing
Measured, not drawn from memory: the demo’s own matcher.mjs, forth.mjs and regexp.f, driven in Node 24.18 (V8 13.6, arm64) against a copy of forth/wasm/tabulate.wast
whose $next loop calls an imported trace(cfa, ip, sp, rsp). Tiers from %IsTurboFanFunction; machine code from --print-wasm-code on the unmodified forth.wasm.
